name: The Fool
upright: A leap into the unknown with an open heart. New journeys start here; trust the path even before it is visible. Carry little, stay curious and let the adventure teach you.
reversed: Recklessness or hesitation at the cliff edge. Check that freedom is not becoming carelessness, or that fear is not stopping a needed start. The cure is to look once before you step, then go anyway if the path is true.
goldenDawn: Aleph, path 11
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Fresh romance or a playful reset in an existing bond.
atWork: A new role, startup idea or career leap worth exploring.
spirit: Beginner's mind is your most sacred tool right now.

name: The Magician
upright: You hold every tool you need. Concentrated intention turns ideas into reality, so act with clarity and craft. Gather your tools on the altar of the day: words, skills, contacts and timing.
reversed: Scattered energy, trickery or talent left unused. Watch for manipulation, your own or someone else's. Pause and ask whether your energy matches your words. Focus on one goal and finish it.
goldenDawn: Beth, path 12
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Clear communication makes attraction real; say what you want.
atWork: Pitch, launch, or demonstrate your skill now.
spirit: Ritual and focused will are especially potent; set a clear intention.

name: The High Priestess
upright: Quiet wisdom speaks beneath the surface. Trust dreams, instinct and what is not yet said aloud. Wait, watch and listen rather than force.
reversed: Secrets kept too long or intuition ignored. Surface noise is drowning out your inner voice. Make time for silence, journaling or dreamwork to hear yourself again.
goldenDawn: Gimel, path 13
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Unspoken feelings or a slow-building, private connection.
atWork: Keep plans confidential and trust your read of people.
spirit: Moon rituals, meditation and divination are favored.

name: The Empress
upright: Growth, comfort and creative fertility flourish. Tend your body, your home and your projects, and they bloom. This card blesses gardens, pregnancies, art and anything you nurture into being.
reversed: Creative block, smothering or neglect of self-care. Abundance stalls when you give without receiving. Return to your senses: rest, nature, beauty and receiving care.
goldenDawn: Daleth, path 14
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Warm, sensual love and deepening commitment.
atWork: Creative projects and customer care thrive; abundance grows steadily.
spirit: Honor the earth and your body as sacred.

name: The Emperor
upright: Order, leadership and firm boundaries bring security. Build the framework that protects what you value. Leadership, father figures and institutions may play a role.
reversed: Rigidity, domination or a lack of discipline. Power is being misused or responsibility avoided. Ask whether your rules protect people or just control them.
goldenDawn: Heh, path 15 (Book T/Golden Dawn; Crowley's Thoth later swaps Heh and Tzaddi)
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Stability and commitment, with care not to dominate.
atWork: Take charge, write the plan, set the policy.
spirit: Build a protective ritual container and keep your practice disciplined.

name: The Hierophant
upright: Wisdom passed down through teachers, lineage and shared rites. Conventional paths or a mentor serve you now. Ceremony, initiation and commitment carry weight now.
reversed: Questioning dogma or breaking from tradition. Seek your own spiritual authority, but beware empty rebellion. Honor what is wise in tradition while letting go of what no longer fits.
goldenDawn: Vav, path 16
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Formal commitment, marriage, or shared values.
atWork: Institutions, credentials and mentors open doors.
spirit: Seek a teacher or study a lineage deeply.

name: The Lovers
upright: A meaningful bond or a choice made from the heart. Align relationships with your deepest values. Love here is a mirror of who you are choosing to become.
reversed: Imbalance, temptation or a values clash. A decision is being avoided or a partnership is out of tune. Return to honest conversation and choose what you can stand behind.
goldenDawn: Zayin, path 17
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Soulmate energy, union and mutual choice.
spirit: Align heart and higher self; sacred union within.

name: The Chariot
upright: Discipline harnesses opposing forces toward triumph. Move forward with determination. Victory comes from steering, not from speed alone.
reversed: Loss of direction or forcing outcomes. Competing desires pull you off course. Get clear on where you are going before pushing harder.
goldenDawn: Cheth, path 18
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Taking the lead in pursuing love; overcoming obstacles together.
atWork: Ambition pays off; travel or a competitive win.
spirit: Willpower in service of spirit; protect your forward path.

name: Strength
upright: Gentle courage tames wild forces. Soft strength and patience achieve what force cannot. Treat your fears and instincts kindly and they become allies.
reversed: Self-doubt, raw impulse or burnout. Reconnect with your inner steadiness before reacting. Rebuild confidence through small acts of courage and rest.
goldenDawn: Teth, path 19 (Waite numbers it 8)
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Patient, devoted love that softens hard edges.
atWork: Steady perseverance and calm leadership win.
spirit: Heart-centered courage; protection through compassion.

name: The Hermit
upright: Step back to seek inner light. Retreat, study and reflection reveal the next step. A guide or teacher may appear, or you may become one.
reversed: Isolation that has become loneliness, or refusing counsel. Return from withdrawal when ready. Balance solitude with connection; share the light you've found.
goldenDawn: Yod, path 20
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Time alone to know what you truly want.
spirit: Inner pilgrimage, retreat, quiet devotion.

name: Wheel of Fortune
upright: The wheel turns in your favor. Cycles shift and timely chances appear; move with the change. Luck favors the prepared; position yourself for the upswing.
reversed: A run of setbacks or resisting inevitable change. What goes down will rise again. Look for the pattern in what keeps repeating, and change your part.
goldenDawn: Kaph, path 21
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Fated meetings and turning points.
atWork: A lucky break or change in fortunes.
spirit: Karma and cycles; flow with the turning.

name: Justice
upright: Truth and fair dealing prevail. Decisions, contracts and legal matters resolve according to merit. Act with integrity and outcomes will balance.
reversed: Unfairness, bias or avoiding accountability. Look honestly at your part in the outcome. Make amends where needed and seek fair counsel.
goldenDawn: Lamed, path 22 (Waite numbers it 11)
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Honest, balanced partnership; mutual accountability.
atWork: Contracts, legal matters and fair outcomes.
spirit: Karmic balance; truth as protection.

name: The Hanged Man
upright: A willing pause reveals a new view. Letting go of control brings insight. What looks like delay may be a necessary incubation.
reversed: Stalling, martyrdom or pointless delay. Stop waiting and release what keeps you suspended. Choose: either surrender fully or move, but stop hovering.
goldenDawn: Mem, path 23
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Seeing a partner differently; pausing to understand.
atWork: A project on hold; new strategy from a new angle.
spirit: Surrender, meditation and seeing from the other side.

name: Death
upright: A chapter closes so a new one can begin. Clear away the old with grace; this is transformation rather than literal death. Grieve what ends and make space for what is coming.
reversed: Resisting change or stagnation. Clinging to what is finished delays renewal. Ask what you are afraid to release, then loosen your grip.
goldenDawn: Nun, path 24
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: A relationship transforms or an old pattern ends.
atWork: Restructuring, a role ends, a new chapter begins.
spirit: Rebirth; cord cutting and shedding the old skin.

name: Temperance
upright: Blend opposites with patience. Moderation and steady flow bring healing. An angelic, steady presence guides the blend of elements.
reversed: Excess, imbalance or impatience. Realign before extremes cause harm. Slow down and restore balance in diet, rest and emotion.
goldenDawn: Samekh, path 25
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Harmonious, patient love; healing between partners.
spirit: Alchemy of spirit and body; healing baths and balance.

name: The Devil
upright: Bonds of habit, desire or fear hold you. Name the chains to see that they can be lifted. Awareness is the first step toward freedom.
reversed: Breaking free and reclaiming power. Release from an unhealthy pattern is near. Keep cutting cords and choose healthier pleasures.
goldenDawn: Ayin, path 26
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Intense attraction, obsession or codependence.
atWork: Golden handcuffs; examine what keeps you stuck.
spirit: Shadow work and naming your fears to reclaim power.

name: The Tower
upright: Sudden change shakes false structures down. Painful as it is, it clears room for truth. What falls was not built on truth; what remains is yours.
reversed: Averting disaster or fearing a needed collapse. Inner upheaval that has not yet been faced. Let the shake-up happen consciously rather than resisting it.
goldenDawn: Peh, path 27
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: A sudden revelation or breakup clears the air.
spirit: Lightning-flash awakening; strong protection and cleansing needed.

name: The Star
upright: Calm and hope return after the storm. Healing flows and your guiding light reappears. Trust that you are guided and keep pouring out your gifts.
reversed: Discouragement or lost faith. Reconnect with small sources of hope. Rest, cleanse and let small hopes rebuild your faith.
goldenDawn: Tzaddi, path 28 (Book T; Crowley later swaps with The Emperor)
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Healing love and renewed hope after hurt.
atWork: Inspired creative work; recognition for your gifts.
spirit: Wishes, star magic and renewal of faith.

name: The Moon
upright: Not all is as it seems. Move gently through uncertainty and let intuition and dreams guide you. Dreams and symbols carry messages; keep a journal.
reversed: Fog lifting and fears released, or deception coming to light. A moonlit cleansing or a frank conversation helps the fog burn off. Name what you fear; truth is easier than the shadows.
goldenDawn: Qoph, path 29
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Uncertainty or hidden feelings; trust slowly.
spirit: Moon magic, dreamwork and psychic protection.

name: The Sun
upright: Warmth, success and pure vitality. Things become clear and joy is shared openly. Children, play and success shine brightly.
reversed: Temporary clouds or diminished enthusiasm. The light is still there, only dimmed. Choose gratitude and the light returns quickly.
goldenDawn: Resh, path 30
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Happy, open, warm love; celebration.
spirit: Solar blessing; vitality and joy as spiritual practice.

name: Judgement
upright: A call to rise and answer your purpose. Reflection brings release and rebirth. Forgive the past and rise into your purpose.
reversed: Self-doubt, harsh self-judgment or ignoring the call. Release old guilt so you can hear what is asking for you. Answer the call in small ways; you are ready.
goldenDawn: Shin, path 31
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Second chances and honest reckonings.
atWork: A calling, a promotion, or a major decision.
spirit: Spiritual awakening and rebirth.

name: The World
upright: A cycle completes in fulfillment. Celebrate the achievement and integration. Travel, achievement and a sense of wholeness are favored.
reversed: Loose ends or the lack of closure. One last step remains before completion. Finish what you started and celebrate the close.
goldenDawn: Tav, path 32
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Fulfilled, mature love; a cycle complete.
spirit: Integration and union with the whole.

name: Ace of Wands
upright: A burst of creative fire and fresh drive. A new venture, passion or idea is ready to be seized. Say yes while the energy is fresh and give it a first concrete step.
reversed: Delays, false starts or a spark without fuel. Wait until the energy is real before committing. Sometimes the idea is right but the timing is not. Gather fuel before you light it again.
astrology: Root of the powers of Fire
goldenDawn: Ace: Kether; Fire signs: Aries, Leo, Sagittarius
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: A sudden spark of attraction or renewed desire.
atWork: A new project, pitch or business idea with real heat.
spirit: Light a candle for a fresh intention and act on it the same day.

name: Two of Wands
upright: You survey the horizon with the world in your hand. Plan boldly and decide where to expand. Weigh staying in comfort against reaching for something bigger.
reversed: Fear of the unknown or plans stuck at the drawing board. Comfort may be holding you back from a bolder plan. Decide, or the window may close.
goldenDawn: Lord of Dominion; sephirah Chokmah
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Deciding whether a relationship can grow beyond its current walls.
atWork: Long-range planning, expansion or a move abroad.
spirit: Map your spiritual goals and choose a direction.

name: Three of Wands
upright: Ships are sailing in. Early efforts begin to pay off and wider horizons open. Look ahead with confidence, because what you launched is gaining ground.
reversed: Obstacles in expansion or disappointment that help has not arrived. Expect a slower return than hoped. Check the plan and be patient with partners far away.
goldenDawn: Lord of Established Strength; sephirah Binah
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: A long-distance bond or a relationship ready to expand.
atWork: Exports, travel, partnerships and growth beyond local markets.
spirit: Widen your perspective; study traditions beyond your own.

name: Four of Wands
upright: A joyful milestone and a secure foundation. Celebrate with community and home. Weddings, homecomings and community events are favored.
reversed: Tension at home or a celebration delayed, though the foundation remains. The joy is there, but transition or family friction clouds it. Look for the root and celebrate anyway.
goldenDawn: Lord of Perfected Work; sephirah Chesed
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Engagement, moving in together or a joyful milestone.
atWork: A finished phase worth celebrating with the team.
spirit: Home blessings, threshold rituals and gratitude.

name: Five of Wands
upright: Clashing egos and lively rivalry. Struggle can sharpen you if it stays fair. Keep the competition playful and productive.
reversed: Avoiding conflict, or friction finally settling down. Tension may be going underground rather than resolving. Name the conflict so it can end.
goldenDawn: Lord of Strife; sephirah Geburah
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Bickering or rivalry; find shared goals.
spirit: Use friction as fuel; channel it into movement or dance.

name: Six of Wands
upright: Public success and well-earned praise. Ride forward with pride. Let others celebrate you without false modesty.
reversed: Fall from grace, ego, or recognition that has not yet come. Do not let validation become your only fuel. Your worth holds even without the parade.
goldenDawn: Lord of Victory; sephirah Tiphareth
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Being admired and proud of a partner.
atWork: Promotion, award or a public success.
spirit: Gratitude rituals; honor your own victories.

name: Seven of Wands
upright: Hold your ground against challenge. Courage and conviction win the higher position. You may feel outnumbered, but the high ground is yours.
reversed: Overwhelm or giving up a position worth holding. Not every fight is worth it, though some ground is worth holding. Choose deliberately.
goldenDawn: Lord of Valour; sephirah Netzach
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Defending a relationship from outside pressure.
atWork: Standing up for your ideas against critics or competitors.
spirit: Protection work for your convictions and boundaries.

name: Eight of Wands
upright: Things move fast; messages and travel arrive. Act while momentum is high. Messages, plans and travel line up quickly.
reversed: Delays, scattered haste or crossed wires. Hurry may cause mistakes or miscommunication. Slow the pace and confirm details.
goldenDawn: Lord of Swiftness; sephirah Hod
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Fast romance or messages flying back and forth.
atWork: Rapid progress, quick decisions, travel for business.
spirit: Swift manifestation; keep your intentions clear.

name: Nine of Wands
upright: Wounded but still standing, with the finish line near. Guard your boundaries one more round. Rest your wounds but keep your guard up for the last stretch.
reversed: Exhaustion or paranoia. Rest before the defensiveness hardens. Rigid defensiveness can hurt more than it protects. Let trusted people in.
goldenDawn: Lord of Great Strength; sephirah Yesod
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Hesitance after past hurt; trust slowly.
atWork: Persistence through a tough final phase.
spirit: Protection rituals and energetic boundaries.

name: Ten of Wands
upright: Carrying too much alone. Success has brought heavy obligations. You may be the only one carrying it, but you need not be.
reversed: Setting down burdens and delegating. Release what is not yours to carry. Ask for help before your back breaks.
goldenDawn: Lord of Oppression; sephirah Malkuth
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Carrying the emotional load; share the weight.
atWork: Overwork; time to delegate and prioritize.
spirit: Release ritual; set down old obligations.

name: Page of Wands
upright: An eager messenger of new ideas and adventures. Curiosity opens doors. A bold message, a creative invitation or a fresh hobby arrives.
reversed: Hasty plans or news that falls flat. Ideas without follow-through fizzle. Choose one and test it.
astrology: Earth of Fire; rules a quadrant of heaven around the North Pole
goldenDawn: Princess (Waite: Page) of Wands
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Flirty, playful and enthusiastic energy.
atWork: An internship, trial run or creative pitch.
spirit: A new spiritual curiosity calls; explore it.

name: Knight of Wands
upright: Charging forward with fiery passion. Travel, a bold move or a sudden change of residence. Expect adventure, travel or a dramatic change of scene.
reversed: Impulsiveness, recklessness or scattered energy. Restless energy can burn bridges. Aim before you charge.
astrology: Fire of Fire; last decan of Scorpio to first two of Sagittarius
goldenDawn: Lord/King of the steed (Waite: Knight) of Wands
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Passionate pursuit; watch for fickleness.
spirit: Fire energy rising; move your body in ritual.

name: Queen of Wands
upright: A vibrant, magnetic presence who leads with warmth. Own your power with joy. Your confidence lights up a room and draws others in.
reversed: Jealousy, insecurity or temper flaring. Insecurity can turn into jealousy or control. Return to self-trust.
astrology: Water of Fire; last decan of Pisces to first two of Aries
goldenDawn: Queen of the throne of Wands
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Warm, confident and magnetic attraction.
spirit: Sunlight rituals, candle work and self-confidence charms.

name: King of Wands
upright: A visionary leader who inspires others to act. Take charge of the big picture. Think big and lead from purpose.
reversed: Arrogance, impatience or high expectations that are not met. Big visions need patience with the people carrying them out. Listen more and dictate less.
astrology: Air of Fire; last decan of Cancer to first two of Leo
goldenDawn: Prince of the chariot (Waite: King) of Wands
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: A bold, committed and protective partner.
spirit: Lead your own spiritual path with vision.

name: Ace of Cups
upright: An overflowing cup of love, intuition and spiritual blessing. The heart opens to new feeling. Receive affection, creativity or spiritual grace with an open heart.
reversed: Emotional blockage or love held back. Tend your own cup first. Love may be blocked, or kept to yourself. Fill your own cup before pouring out.
astrology: Root of the powers of Water
goldenDawn: Ace: Kether; Water signs: Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: New love or deep emotional renewal.
spirit: Spiritual gifts and intuition open.

name: Two of Cups
upright: Two hearts meet as equals. Romance, friendship or a healing reconciliation. Connection rooted in respect is offered.
reversed: Disharmony or a broken connection between partners. A rift or imbalance needs honest repair. Reach out first.
goldenDawn: Lord of Love; sephirah Chokmah
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Mutual attraction; a soul-level bond.
spirit: Sacred partnership; heart-to-heart healing.

name: Three of Cups
upright: Joyful gatherings, sisterhood and shared happiness. Celebrate your circle. Celebrate your people and let joy flow.
reversed: Overindulgence, gossip or feeling left out. Too much partying, or friends taking sides. Balance social time with real connection.
goldenDawn: Lord of Abundance; sephirah Binah
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Joyful socializing; love found among friends.
spirit: Circle work, group rituals and sisterhood.

name: Four of Cups
upright: Turned inward, you may overlook an offered gift. Reflect, but notice what is being held out to you. Notice the offer before you dismiss it.
reversed: Waking from apathy and saying yes to new chances. Fresh motivation returns after a numb spell. Accept the chance now.
goldenDawn: Lord of Blended Pleasure; sephirah Chesed
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Boredom; look again at what's on offer.
spirit: Meditation; stay open to subtle signs.

name: Five of Cups
upright: Mourning what spilled. Yet two cups still stand behind you. Grieve what was lost, then turn toward what remains.
reversed: Acceptance, forgiveness and moving on. The worst of the grief is lifting. Forgive and walk toward the bridge.
goldenDawn: Lord of Loss in Pleasure; sephirah Geburah
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Heartbreak or regret; healing begins.
spirit: Grief rituals and emotional release.

name: Six of Cups
upright: Sweet memories, childhood joy and kind exchanges. The past offers comfort. Old friends, childhood places or gentle gifts return.
reversed: Stuck in the past, or ready to grow beyond it. Living in the past may be blocking the present. Honor memories and move on.
goldenDawn: Lord of Pleasure; sephirah Tiphareth
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Rekindled love or innocent affection.
atWork: Returning to old skills, mentors or clients.
spirit: Inner-child healing and ancestor gratitude.

name: Seven of Cups
upright: Many dazzling options, not all real. Ground your wishes before choosing. Separate fantasy from real opportunity.
reversed: Clarity emerges and illusions dissolve. The mist lifts and real choices emerge. Commit to one.
goldenDawn: Lord of Illusionary Success; sephirah Netzach
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Idealizing someone; see clearly.
spirit: Visualization and vision work, grounded with action.

name: Eight of Cups
upright: Leaving behind what no longer fulfils you. A spiritual quest begins. It takes courage to leave what is good but no longer right.
reversed: Fear of leaving or aimless drifting. You may hesitate at the threshold. Ask what would make leaving or staying truly worth it.
goldenDawn: Lord of Abandoned Success; sephirah Hod
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Walking away from what no longer fulfils.
atWork: Leaving a role for deeper meaning.
spirit: Pilgrimage, solitude and spiritual seeking.

name: Nine of Cups
upright: The wish card: comfort, pleasure and satisfaction are granted. Share the good fortune and let yourself be pleased. Enjoy what you have achieved without guilt.
reversed: Smugness or a wish that does not satisfy. Satisfaction may hide a deeper longing. Ask what you truly wish for.
goldenDawn: Lord of Material Happiness; sephirah Yesod
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Contentment and wishes coming true.
atWork: Satisfaction with results; a bonus or recognition.
spirit: Gratitude; make a heartfelt wish.

name: Ten of Cups
upright: Lasting joy, a loving home and shared happiness under the rainbow. Gather your people and appreciate the shelter you share. Love, family and home feel whole.
reversed: Family tension or idealized expectations. Family friction or unmet expectations disturb the peace. Value what is real over the picture-perfect.
goldenDawn: Lord of Perfected Success; sephirah Malkuth
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: Lasting partnership and family joy.
spirit: Ancestral blessings and home harmony.

name: Page of Cups
upright: A dreamy messenger with a surprising emotional offer. Play with intuition. Expect a sweet surprise, a creative idea or an intuitive nudge.
reversed: Emotional immaturity or creative block. Feelings may be immature or blocked. Let yourself feel without drama.
astrology: Earth of Water; rules a quadrant of heaven around the North Pole
goldenDawn: Princess (Waite: Page) of Cups
source: Paraphrased from Waite (1910) and Golden Dawn Book T (archive.org transcription); decans/court spans verified against Book T. Original wording.
inLove: A tender confession or new feelings.
spirit: Dream journaling and intuitive play.

name: Knight of Cups
upright: An invitation, proposal or romantic quest. Follow the heart with grace. Follow beauty and feeling, but keep your feet on the ground.
reversed: Moodiness, unrealistic romance or broken promises. Charm without substance disappoints. Look for actions behind the words.
astrology: Fire of Water; last decan of Aquarius to first two of Pisces
goldenDawn: Lord/King of the steed (Waite: Knight) of Cups

name: Ace of Swords
upright: A cutting insight or decisive truth. Mental clarity breaks through confusion. Use it to cut through confusion and state the truth.
reversed: Confusion, misused words or a harsh truth handled badly. Thoughts are muddled or words are being used carelessly. Pause until you can speak clearly.

name: Two of Swords
upright: A blindfolded truce between two options. Something must be faced to move on. Remove the blindfold, listen to your intuition and decide.
reversed: Information comes to light and the stalemate breaks. Information breaks the stalemate. Choose, even if imperfectly.

name: Three of Swords
upright: Painful truth pierces the heart. Allow grief so healing can start. The pain is real; let it be felt.
reversed: Recovery, release and forgiveness. Old hurts are slowly healing. Forgive yourself and others as you can.

name: Four of Swords
upright: Withdraw to recover strength. Meditation and quiet heal the mind. Rest is not idleness; it is preparation.

goldenDawn: Lord of Rest from Strife; sephirah Chesed

spirit: Spiritual journey and gradual healing.
